Question Choices: Classify 4(x + 2) = 4x + 8 as having one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
Hints: Distribute the left side and compare both sides.
Solution: The left side becomes 4x + 8, identical to the right side, so every real x is a solution.

Question Choices: Classify 3(2x - 1) = 6x + 5 as having one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
Hints: Distribute 3 and see what happens to the x-terms.
Solution: The equation becomes 6x - 3 = 6x + 5. Subtracting 6x gives -3 = 5, which is false, so there is no solution.

Question Choices: Classify 5x + 7 = 5x + 7 as having one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
Solution: The equation is true for every real x, so it has infinitely many solutions.

Question Choices: Classify 2(x + 3) = 2x + 7 as having one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions.
Solution: The equation becomes 2x + 6 = 2x + 7. Removing 2x gives 6 = 7, so there is no solution.
